content.title: About
content.content: Rice cake is a light, crunchy snack made from whole grain rice, usually formed into thin round discs. It is gluten‑free, low in calories, and has a neutral taste, making it popular among health‑conscious consumers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice cakes originated in Japan in the early 20th century as a convenient way to preserve rice.
They are often used in Asian cuisine as a base for toppings such as soy sauce, avocado, or smoked salmon.
Their porous structure quickly absorbs sauces and marinades.
There are many flavored versions: sea‑salt, caramel, chocolate, and even with added seeds.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: A typical serving (≈10 g) contains about 35 kcal, making it a good alternative to higher‑calorie snacks.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Provides slowly digestible energy, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Practically fat‑free, which is beneficial for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains small amounts of B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides trace amounts of thiamine and niacin that support metabolism.

items.title: Low protein content
items.content: Rice cakes are not a significant source of protein and should not replace protein‑rich foods.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Some flavored varieties are heavily salted; choose low‑sodium options if you monitor salt intake.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: Rare, but individuals with a rice allergy should avoid them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat rice cakes plain, spread with nut butter, hummus, avocado, or use as a base for canapés. They can also be crumbled into salads for added crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight package in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, refrigerate to prevent moisture absorption, which makes the cake soft.
